Frequently asked questions
+
Does Trello offer a Premium free trial?
We sure do. All users can enroll their Workspace in a
free trial of Trello Premium
. With that trial your Workspace will get access to create unlimited Trello boards, automate as much as you’d like, take advantage of Timeline, Dashboard, and other new views, and much more!
+
Do you offer any discounted plans?
Yes! Trello offers both a
non-profit community discount
as well as an
education discount
.
+
What payment methods do you accept?
You can purchase a monthly or annual Trello Standard or Premium subscription with any major credit card. We offer more options for Enterprise customers, if you’re interested in learning more about Trello Enterprise
contact our sales team.
+
How do I cancel my Trello Standard or Premium subscription?
If you aren’t 100% satisfied with Trello Standard or Premium you may downgrade at any time. When a team downgrades from Standard or Premium, it retains its Standard or Premium features and unlimited boards until the end of its prepaid service period. At the end of its prepaid service period, it becomes a free Trello Workspace that can hold 10 boards. Learn more about canceling your Standard or Premium subscription
here.
+
How are users counted towards billing?
A Trello user who is added as a member to a Workspace—either as a normal member or as a team admin—is considered a billable team member that is included in the cost of Trello Standard or Premium.
Any Guest that is on more than one board within the Workspace is considered a Multi-Board Guest and is billed at the same rate as Standard or Premium Workspace members.
See this page
for more information on Multi-Board Guests.
+
Is there an on-premises version of Trello?
Trello is proudly a cloud-only product. We offer access via the web, desktop, and our
awesome mobile apps
.
+
Can I have Trello Standard or Premium just for my own account?
Trello Standard and Premium are designed for all teams—even teams of one! To upgrade to Standard or Premium you’ll need to create a Workspace and then upgrade that Workspace.
+
How secure is Trello?
Trello, Inc. (“we”, “us” or “our”) is SOC2 Type 2 certified—we receive and review our data hosting providers’ SOC1 and SOC2 reports every 6 months under NDA. Trello is ISO/IEC 27001 certified which validates our information security management system (ISMS) and the implementation of our security controls. More information is available on the Atlassian Trust Management System. Trello is PCI-DSS certified. Learn more about Trello’s security protocols
here
.

Frequently asked questions
What is an AI request?
An AI request is one successful unit of work executed by AI Teammates or Asana Dash, which share a single pool of AI requests. Administrative tasks in Dash are included at no extra cost. You're only charged when work gets done; failed, timed-out, or canceled tasks don't count.
For Dash, AI requests only count when Dash completes complex work (e.g., integrations, web search, long-form content generation) or hands off the work to an AI Teammate.
What is the contract term for my paid AI requests?
Paid usage packs are valid for your entire billing cycle. For monthly customers: packs expire at month's end. For annual customers: packs can be used anytime across your contract term with no monthly resets. On-demand, pay-as-you-go billing is also available, billed monthly for exactly what you used with no upfront commitment.
How do I purchase additional AI requests?
You have two options. Prepaid usage packs at $0.50 per request, valid for your full billing cycle. On-demand, pay-as-you-go billing at $0.60 per request, billed monthly in arrears.
How do I monitor and control my costs?
Your admin console shows a live dashboard of requests consumed, remaining balance, and usage by user and AI Teammate. Alerts fire at 65%, 85%, and 100% of your allotment. Admins can set a spending cap on on-demand billing and toggle AI request access per user at any time.
Can I change or cancel my plan?
You can cancel at any time, and if you cancel before your next renewal, you'll retain access to paid features through the end of your current subscription period. To cancel your paid plan, log in to your Asana account and access your admin console.
How many users are included in my plan?
Asana offers flexible subscription options based on the features you need and the size of your team. For smaller teams, we have plans designed for 2 members.
How is AI Studio priced?
AI Studio is available on Starter, Advanced, Enterprise, and Enterprise+ plans.
AI Studio is available in three options:
AI Studio Basic:
Included access to AI Studio to explore how AI can help take on routine, manual work (includes rate limits).
AI Studio Plus:
Paid access to AI Studio to level up productivity for individuals and small teams (available on monthly & annual plans).
AI Studio Pro:
Paid access to AI Studio to scale complex workflows and business operations with advanced billing controls (available on an annual plan).
To get started, ensure your admin has Asana AI enabled. From there, all members of your domain will be able to build smart workflows.
Learn more here
.
How can I add people to my plan?
You can grow your team by adding seats in increments as follows:
Between 2 and 5 total users:
add seats in increments of 1
Up to 30 total users:
add seats in increments of 5
Up to 100 total users:
add seats in increments of 10
Up to 500 total users:
add seats in increments of 25
More than 500 users:
add seats in increments of 50
How secure is Asana?
Asana is committed to protecting customer data. We build our platform using best practices for highly available, scalable, and secure cloud applications. We regularly monitor and assess our program to ensure that it meets or exceeds compliance and regulatory requirements. Please visit our
Trust Center
for more information.
Do you offer academic pricing?
We’re happy to work with student groups using Asana.
Contact us
.
Should I upgrade my organization or my team?
If you need administrators and premium package features for all teams, upgrade your entire organization. If you don't need administrators or premium features for all teams, but want to add more guests, set per-project permissions, or hide a team, you can upgrade an individual team.
Learn more
.
Will I be charged sales tax?
Yes. We will apply state and local sales tax based on your billing address to your total charge.
Is there an on-premises version of Asana?
We are passionate about the web and do not plan to offer an internally hosted version of Asana.
How does Asana protect my data?
Asana is committed to protecting and honoring your global privacy rights as well as securing the data you provide to us through the use of our products. For more information and details about our privacy and security programs, please visit our
Trust Center
.
How does Asana store my data?
The Asana subscription service is hosted on dedicated servers within secure, industry-leading data centers provided by Amazon Web Services. These data centers have achieved and maintain SOC 2 compliance and provide 24-hour physical security including biometric access controls and continuous surveillance.
Will I be charged VAT/GST?
Asana may be required to charge VAT, GST, and other taxes on your subscription in accordance with local laws and regulations. Some jurisdictions do not require VAT/GST to be charged if the purchaser is registered for VAT/GST. If you are registered for VAT or GST purposes, please add your VAT/GST registration number during the checkout process to have your exemption processed. For more information, please visit our Asana VAT Help
page
.
Does Asana offer a discount for nonprofits?
Asana is happy to offer eligible nonprofit organizations a discount on an Asana Starter or Asana Advanced annual plan. You can learn about the
Asana nonprofit discount here
.
What is your refund policy?
We do not offer refunds. If you cancel your plan before the next renewal cycle, you will retain access to paid features until the end of your subscription period. When your subscription expires, you will lose access to paid features and all data associated with those features.

How to Choose the Best ClickUp Pricing Plan For You
Jeff Cypher
Productivity Professor, ZenPilot
Last updated September 2, 2026
So, you’ve decided to go with
ClickUp
as the project management tool for your team? Great choice. But wait - which ClickUp pricing plan do you need?
What features do you really need versus what are just nice to haves?
And, is there a plan that will magically solve all my problems? (I can answer that last one quickly - no.)
In this article, I’ll break down some of the key feature differences and when you might want to upgrade to the next pricing tier based on your preferences and needs.
One thing has changed since this article was first written: you can now
buy ClickUp licenses through ZenPilot
at ClickUp’s official rates. Same plans, same prices, plus a team that has implemented ClickUp 3,100+ times helping you pick. More on that at the end.
ClickUp Pricing Plans: Key Feature Differences
As of 2026, ClickUp’s pricing page shows four plans. A fifth is still available even though it no longer appears there. The five ClickUp pricing plans are:
Free Forever
Unlimited
Business
Business Plus (no longer on the public pricing page, but still available as an upgrade and through partners like ZenPilot)
Enterprise
On top of any paid plan, ClickUp sells AI as separate per-seat add-ons: ClickUp Brain and Everything AI. We’ll cover those after the core plans.
Let’s spend some time looking at each of these plans to determine which plan your team will need and when you may need to upgrade.
The Free Forever Plan
If you’ve already decided to implement ClickUp for your team, then you more than likely already have a Free account setup.
The great thing about the Free plan is that you get all the basic features you’d need to try out the core functionality. Many tools gate access with a limited trial and then don’t let you access the tool until you pay. Not so with ClickUp.
Some features that are available (and useful) for agencies out of the box are:
Unlimited tasks and members
Two-Factor Authentication
Collaborative Docs
Kanban Boards
Smart Notifications
Embed Views - allows you to embed Google spreadsheets, presentations, documents, etc.
Native Time Tracking
Having unlimited tasks and free plan members is a huge plus to be able to try out the platform exhaustively. But the free plan only gets you so far.
Why we don’t recommend the Free Forever Plan for agencies
If you plan to upload assets (especially creative ones) to the platform for reviews and approvals, then you’ll quickly bump up against the 60MB storage limitation. A single Photoshop file could reach that limit!
This plan also lacks the ability to add things like a Form for managing work requests. We’re big on simplifying workflows and forms help with that.
The free plan has a Custom Field limit that also hinders the progress of agencies. Custom fields are the building blocks of any professional ClickUp system.
As an agency operator, we don’t recommend you stay on the Free Forever Plan once you’ve decided to move your agency operations to ClickUp. It’s simply not robust enough.
The Unlimited Plan
At $7 per member per month (billed annually), Unlimited is a great choice to expand ClickUp’s capabilities, especially on the Storage front. Here are some key differences from the Free plan:
Unlimited Storage (quite the jump from 60MB)
Unlimited Integrations - so you can integrate with all the tools you need.
Guests with Permissions - this is great for your part-time freelancer or clients that you invite into ClickUp.
Unlimited Custom Fields. We’re huge fans of segmenting and structuring work and views using custom fields. Not having a limit here is a big deal.
Column Calculations, for being able to add up the total time estimates of tasks for a given day or timeframe, among other use cases.
Email in ClickUp. This is great for when you want to email vendors or clients for things like welcome emails, feedback on assets, etc.
The Unlimited Plan is great if you’re a very small team and need to keep a close watch on all your expenses to make sure you don’t enter software bloat (it’s a real thing).
Cash flow is king for young startups so it could make sense to park your team on the Unlimited plan.
Why we don’t recommend the Unlimited Plan for agencies
However, if you decided to use the Unlimited Plan, you’d be missing out on some very important features that we (at ZenPilot) find crucial to managing your operation within ClickUp.
You get access to forms on the Unlimited plan, but you can’t brand them or customize them very well.
You do get unlimited tasks, spaces, and views, but ClickUp sets a limit on the number of lists and folders per space (200 for each, to be exact). Funny, given the name is Unlimited, it does actually have
limits.
You also can’t publicly share any views from the Everything level (which should be done sparingly, but limiting nonetheless).
Additionally, low automation limits, with only 1000 operations/month - and you cannot add multiple Actions or Conditions - are major inhibitors.
99.9% of the time, we don’t recommend agencies use the Free Forever Plan or the Unlimited Plan.
So let’s get down to “Business” (pun intended).
The Business Plan
If you were to work with us at ZenPilot on a
ClickUp implementation
, the Business Plan is a non-negotiable item. At a bare minimum, your team must absolutely be on the Business plan.
The Business Plan will run you $12 per member per month billed annually, or $19 per member month to month.
The increase in cost gets you a very crucial function of the platform:
Workload Management
I could mention some other features like Custom Exporting or Advanced Public Sharing (both important additions), but nothing comes close to the importance of being able to manage your team’s resources with the Workload view in ClickUp.
At ZenPilot, we’re quite prescriptive and opinionated about how teams run on ClickUp. That’s partly because one of the key complaints we hear from agencies all day every day is that they have no visibility into who’s doing what and when and who’s being held accountable for those things. (If you’re curious what’s changed recently, check out our
ClickUp 4.0 review
.)
No longer must that be true!
With our methodology and ClickUp’s Workload Management view, you will now be able to see the total number of tasks assigned to someone on a given day and a summary of the time estimates of those tasks (as long as you’re following our rule of every task getting an assignee, a due date, and a time estimate).
The Workload view is critical in getting a global perspective on your team’s committed work and output. It also makes it much easier to spot when people have been overloaded with work.
That’s all great and dandy, but why does that matter?
By knowing exactly where and how your resources are dedicated, this gives you as an agency owner or operator the ability to properly staff your team. No more do you have to guess if your team is actually overloaded or if they’re just low capacity people. Many teams are overburdened and are understaffed. But the opposite is also true, maybe just as often - teams are overstaffed and have way more overhead than they need because they’re not properly tracking the team’s workload.

The Business Plus Plan
This plan costs $19 per member per month billed annually. ClickUp removed Business Plus from its public pricing page in late 2024, but it’s still available as an upgrade, and we can quote it for you. For some teams that might feel steep. But the payoff of the additional features can definitely be worth it.
At ZenPilot, we highlight three key features of Business Plus:
Subtasks in Multiple Lists
Conditional Logic in Forms
Custom Capacity in Workload
Allow me to break these three down.
Subtasks in Multiple Lists
This feature might not seem like a big deal, but this can be a game changer depending on your workflow.
What this allows you to do is have a single subtask show up in other lists (duh). Where this can be handy is in a client approval workflow.
Let’s say you have a subtask in your process template that could be assigned to a client, but you don’t want to give the client visibility into everything you’re executing in a given list. Our approach here is to create a Shared Client List that the client has access to, but restrict access to all other lists. Then, from the list where the subtask lives, you can “share” that subtask into that Shared Client List, so now it’s visible in both places, but the client only has access to the task you want them to have.
Or take a Sprint workflow. If you have multiple sprint lists and a master backlog lists, you might choose to have subtasks live in multiple lists so that you have visibility in several places: at the sprint level, at the client level, at the work category level, etc. The options are endless!
Okay one more example: let’s say you’re tracking company goals and you want to be able to visualize all goals by department, team lead, individual contributor, etc. If those goal tasks are setup as subtasks, then they can be shared and viewable in multiple places based on it’s context.
Conditional Logic in Forms
This is a very recent addition to the lineup of features, but a very important one nonetheless. Say goodbye to tools like Typeform or JotForm! Teams would use those tools for their forms because they have conditional logic. I agree that Typeform forms are a thing of beauty (and we use their other tool call VideoAsk for video surveys and such for its UX and ease of use), but in an effort to create your team’s single source-of-truth, it is now no longer necessary to use an external forms tool. ClickUp can now serve as the centralized platform for all your form needs.
By using the conditional logic available in ClickUp Forms, you can create branches based on the answers someone is giving on a form that they fill out.
For development teams, you can now use a single form to capture both Feature Requests and Bug Reports based on what the form filler designates. This simplifies the number of forms teams would need to manage to house incoming work requests.
You can also use conditional logic in Client Work Request forms. No more need for rambly emails from clients asking for random assets that you may or may not provide. Just point them to your Work Request Form and funnel that request accordingly.
Bravo, team.
Custom Capacity in Workload
If you’re a growing agency then you’re probably utilizing freelancers and contractors that don’t work a normal full-time 40-hour week for you. That’s good for books, but bad for your workload management if you’re on a lower ClickUp plan.
With the custom capacity feature, you can now designate exactly how many hours someone is available to work for you in the Workload view. You can even designate the number of hours by day! So if a freelance designer works 8 hour days Monday, Wednesday, and Friday, but doesn’t work the other days, you can designate that custom capacity in the Workload view if needed.
This allows Team Leads and resource managers to more easily spot when work has been inappropriately assigned or if a limited freelancer has been assigned more work than they’re contractually agreed to.
Game changer.

But what about ClickUp’s Enterprise plan? Is it
ever
worth it? What are the functions and features of ClickUp’s most expensive plan that you should consider as a team?
Believe it or not, Business Plus is actually our 2nd plan choice for agencies and believe the features and functionality of Enterprise is well worth it.
The Enterprise Plan
This is the mother of all ClickUp plans.
The Enterprise Plan is a perfect fit for teams that require more security and permission settings that the lower plans don’t accommodate for.
We’re going to come right out of the gate and recommend this plan for all agencies, no matter your size.
Some notable mentions here are:
Advanced Permissions
Enhanced Security to provide extra levels of authentication through Single-Sign On (SSO) and 2FA (like Google, Azure, Okta, Custom SAML)
MSA & HIPAA certification
Custom Field Manager to ensure data accuracy across the whole workspace (we’re big fans of custom fields so this is a very helpful feature).
White Labeling, so you can add your own logo and colors to brand the ClickUp platform for your team.
Large Automation + API Call Limits
Let’s unpack a couple of these features and discuss why you should be thinking about the Enterprise plan for your team.
Advanced Permissions
Have you ever had a ClickUp doc or a view shared externally by a team member (whether accidentally or on purpose, no judgment here) that shouldn’t have been? With these advanced permission settings, you can now block the ability to publicly share any doc or view in ClickUp. No more accidentally sharing trade secrets or meeting notes! Restrict that access!
You can also restrict who can add guest users to your account. This can help you reign in any unsanctioned activity from your team. You wouldn’t want any third-parties being able to peek at your workflows or documentation without you knowing, would you? Guest seats have very specific use cases and should be determined by the Agency Operator, not by anybody on the team. Restrict that access!
I’ll mention one more function here: being able to block team members from deleting items they didn’t create. We’ve had clients lose entire knowledge bases and SOP documentation because someone “accidentally” deleted it from ClickUp. We’ve also had clients who’ve had team members “accidentally” delete over 50% of their live tasks in ClickUp (I’m not sure how in the world that accidentally happens, but such is life)! This one feature function alone can save you hours of headache in the future. Restrict that access!
Automations + API Calls
If you’re transitioning to ClickUp, then you’re thinking about your productivity. If you’re thinking about productivity, then you’re thinking about automation. And NOTHING is worse that reaching your automation limits prematurely and not having automations run, causing you to miss work, deadlines, follow ups, and the list goes on.
What’s it worth to you as an agency owner or operator to have peace of mind knowing that all your automations and API calls will run without a hitch because you have the maximum limits possible inside ClickUp? I can’t read your mind, but I bet it’s quite valuable.
On the Enterprise Plan, you get 250,000 automations a month! Business Plus caps out at 50,000, and Business is even less at 5,000. The difference between 5,000 and 250,000 is quite large - 245,000, to be precise. That means that you’re 50 times less likely to run out of automations on the Enterprise plan than the Business plan. We think peace of mind is worth the extra cost here.
And how about API calls? The limit here is 10,000 per minute. Business Plus is limited to 1,000 per minute, and Business is limited to 100 per minute. Those are massive differences.
Don’t make a large investment like the energy and cost related to switching your agency to ClickUp and NOT think about the minute details of things like automation limits. Something like that could make or break your retention rate with customers and clients. If one automation fails because of limits that are too low for you, could be the difference between keeping a loyal customer or losing monthly revenue (and a sour taste in a previous client’s mouth - hopefully a mouth that doesn’t like to share their woes).
We believe these extra security measures and features would make Enterprise a no-brainer, even if you are a small team.
As far as pricing, you’ll have to talk to a sales representative from ClickUp to get a quote as it can differ based on your needs and team size (and what discounts they might be willing to offer). But the features of Enterprise are most likely a need and not a want, so the Enterprise plan is what you got to have!
ClickUp AI Add-Ons: Brain and Everything AI
None of the plans above include AI. ClickUp sells it separately, per paid seat, on top of whatever plan you’re on:
ClickUp Brain
at $9 per user per month (billed annually). Unlimited Brain assistant, @Brain agent, and AI chat, plus a monthly pool of AI Super Credits.
Everything AI
at $28 per user per month. Everything in Brain plus unlimited Ambient Answers, the AI Notetaker, image generation, and a much larger credit pool for Super Agents.
AI Super Credits
can be added on top of either tier when your agents, AI fields, and automations burn through the included pool.
Our take: Brain earns its price once your workspace is clean. AI on top of a messy hierarchy just produces confident nonsense faster. Everything AI makes sense for the people running agents and the notetaker every day, not for every seat. Start with Brain, watch the credit usage for a month, then upgrade only the seats that need more. Our
ClickUp AI guide
goes deeper on what each tier actually does.
Buying ClickUp Licenses Through ZenPilot
Whichever plan you land on, you can now buy it through ZenPilot instead of directly from ClickUp. The plans and prices are identical to buying direct. What changes is who’s on the other end of the purchase.
The plan recommendation comes from a team that has implemented ClickUp for 3,100+ clients. If Business does the job, we won’t push you to Enterprise.
Licenses, implementation, training, and support can all sit on one agreement with one invoice.
You get a human to call about seats, add-ons, and renewals before you ever open a ClickUp support ticket.
Licenses are sold on annual terms, and you can buy them on their own or bundled with a block of support hours. The full details are on our

.
Wrapping It Up
To summarize, choosing the right ClickUp plan for your agency ultimately comes down on team size, workflow needs, and budget.
While the free and unlimited plans offer basic functionality to try out ClickUp, they lack key features like workload management that are critical for managing your agency.
The Business plan is the minimum recommended for agencies, but for agencies that need more security, customization, and automation power, the Enterprise plan is the best fit. Its advanced permissions, SSO integration, and huge automation limits provide the flexibility and control required to run an agency efficiently in ClickUp.
While cost is always a factor, choosing too basic of a plan can end up costing you more in productivity and efficiency losses in the long run. Evaluate your team’s needs closely, think through your workflow, and choose the plan that allows ClickUp to work for you rather than against you. Once you’ve picked your plan, the next step is

Whether you manage a small team or handle enterprise-level operations, we’ll explore ClickUp's pricing tiers and find out if the tool is the right for your needs.
ClickUp is a go-to project management tool known for doing it all.
But how do its pricing plans compare: both against each other and the competition? Are there any hidden limitations? And which plan fits your needs best?
In this guide, we’ll explain everything and help you choose the right option before you dive into ClickUp.
ClickUp’s Pricing Plans
ClickUp’s pricing
offers a free plan that includes unlimited task creation, access to 60 MB of storage, and collaborative docs.
The platform has three paid plans with a 14-day free trial:
Unlimited:
Starts at $7 per user/month, which includes access to unlimited custom views, timesheets, guest access, and 100 mind map creations.
Business:
Starts at $12 per user/month and adds private docs, sprint reporting, and all dashboard views.
Enterprise:
Custom price that adds white labelling, enterprise-grade security, and AI features.

ClickUp: Free Plan
ClickUp’s free plan is best suited for personal use as it offers generous features to get the basic project work up and running.
Here’s a rundown of what’s included in ClickUp’s free plan:
60 MB file storage.
Unlimited Tasks
Unlimited Free Plan Members
Two-Factor Authentication
Collaborative Docs
Kanban Boards
Sprint Management
Calendar View
Basic Custom Field Manager
In-App Video Recording
24/7 Support
One standout feature is the no-user limit, meaning you can invite as many members as you want at no additional cost. The downside is that you will have no control over the permissions. Every user will have full access to your workspace.
Another downside is that ClickUp offers advanced features such as whiteboards and dashboards but with a maximum cap. For example, you get only 60 whiteboards and 100 dashboards, pushing users to upgrade to higher plans.
Source:
ClickUp

ClickUp: Unlimited Plan
The unlimited plan starts at a low price of $10 per user/month (billed monthly) and is best suited for small teams. This plan solves the biggest limitation of free plans, i.e., no permission for guests. You can manage permission levels to share your workspaces across stakeholders. Oyster additions include unlimited storage, spaces, and Gantt charts.
User cap for some features still exists, although increased:
Unlimited Spaces, Folders, and Forms
Unlimited Gantt Charts
Unlimited Integrations
Unlimited Storage
Unlimited Custom Fields
Native Time Tracking
Goals & Portfolio Management
Guests With Permission Control
Resource Management
ClickUp Chat
This plan offers a higher degree of customization and advanced features for a comparatively lower per-user fee.

ClickUp: Business Plan
ClickUp positions its business plan as its most preferred plant for medium—to large-sized businesses. In addition to more control over workspace customization, the plan lifts nearly all use caps and offers unlimited whiteboards, mind maps, dashboards, and views.
This plan also offers more sprint and time management features, including sprint reporting, granular time estimates, and goal organization in the folder. It would be the right fit for sprint, or dev-focused teams.
Additional business plan features include:
Unlimited Dashboards with Advanced Cards
Unlimited Message History
Unlimited Activity Views
Unlimited Timeline Views
Webhooks & Automation Integrations
5K Automations Per Month

Enterprise API
250K Automations Per Month

ONES Project
(project management) and ONES Wiki (knowledge base). You can buy them separately, but they’re designed to work together seamlessly. Think of it as a
Jira alternative
that doesn’t force you to add 15 plugins just to get a decent roadmap or a documentation space. And yes, you can deploy it on your own servers—no cloud dependency required.
Why It Was Selected
Most team tools either go too deep on task management and ignore documentation, or they bolt on a wiki that feels like an afterthought. ONES.com treats both as first‑class citizens. I picked it because it solves the core problem none of the other three address well: keeping your project history, specs, and decisions inside the same tool with native, Jira‑grade workflows, all while offering an on‑premise option that IT teams actually respect.
Core Capabilities
Pain:
Your team uses Confluence for docs, Jira for tasks, and some duct tape for alignment. Context switching is killing velocity.
Capability:
ONES Project and ONES Wiki live in the same workspace. You link a requirement spec directly to a subtask, and anyone can jump from a sprint backlog to the full design document without opening a new tab.
Result:
Engineers, PMs, and designers stop hunting for information and start moving work forward.
Pain:
You need advanced workflows like sub‑tasks, blockers, and custom statuses, but Trello is too flat and Asana gets messy with too many dependencies.
Capability:
ONES Project supports Jira‑compatible workflows, custom fields, and automation rules right out of the box. You can mirror a full software development lifecycle—from backlog grooming to release—without a single marketplace add‑on.
Result:
Your process stays rigorous without crumbling under workarounds.
Pain:
Your organization mandates on‑premise or air‑gapped deployment, and neither ClickUp nor Trello nor Asana will install on your servers.
Capability:
ONES.com offers Cloud, On‑Premise, Private Cloud, and SaaS. The on‑premise version includes the same feature set as the cloud.
Result:
Security‑conscious teams in finance, government, or manufacturing can finally run modern project management behind their own firewall.
Pain:
Reporting feels like a side project because you have to export to a spreadsheet or buy a BI plugin.
Capability:
Built‑in reporting includes burn‑down charts, cumulative flow diagrams, and velocity tracking. You can customize dashboards without leaving the platform.
Result:
Sprint reviews and stakeholder updates become a 5‑minute exercise instead of a data‑wrangling nightmare.
Pain:
Sprint planning is chaotic because tasks don’t link back to the original requirements or fixes.
Capability:
Full sprint management with story points, capacity planning, and backlog prioritization. You can trace every user story to the wiki page where it was defined.
Result:
Grooming sessions finally answer “why are we doing this” without a 10‑minute detour.
Pain:
You’re paying for a dozen add‑ons in Jira just to get a decent board view, timeline, and documentation.
Capability:
ONES Project includes multiple board views, Gantt, and a wiki that integrates natively—no plug‑in costs.
Result:
Your tool budget shrinks and your tool stack simplifies.
Pros
Unified PM and wiki reduce context switching
True on‑premise deployment for air‑gapped environments
Jira‑compatible workflows without the plugin tax
Free plan supports up to 30 users with full features
Built‑in reporting and sprint management
Cons
Wiki is a separate purchase if you need standalone knowledge base
Smaller community compared to ClickUp or Asana
Some advanced automation still catching up to ClickUp’s rule engine
Pricing
Free plan: 30 seats, unrestricted features. Paid plans start at $9/user/month. ONES Wiki sold separately. All deployment options—Cloud, On‑Premise, Private Cloud, SaaS—available at the same price tier.
Best For
Teams that need a serious
project management tool
with a native wiki, enterprise‑grade deployment options, and a Jira‑style workflow engine without the vendor lock‑in. Ideal for software teams, product orgs, and any company that can’t put sensitive data in the cloud.
ClickUp
Product Overview
ClickUp is the Swiss Army knife of project management. It packs docs, goals, chat, whiteboards, and more into one platform. You can customize almost anything—from task statuses to dashboard widgets—which makes it a magnet for power users who want to build their own system.
Why It Was Selected
If you’re the type of team that says “I wish my tool could do X,” ClickUp probably already does X. It consistently pushes the envelope on feature breadth, and its “Everything” view lets you see all tasks across all projects, which is a lifesaver for multi‑project managers.
Core Capabilities
Pain:
You manage 20 projects simultaneously and can’t remember which overdue task lives where.
Capability:
The “Everything” view aggregates every task, regardless of space or folder, with powerful filters.
Result:
You catch slipping deadlines before the Monday morning meeting.
Pain:
Your reporting needs are unique, and standard dashboards feel too rigid.
Capability:
Custom dashboards with over 50 widget types let you build exactly the view you need—from team workload to time tracking breakdowns.
Result:
Stakeholders get the metrics they actually care about, not a generic template.
Pain:
You waste hours manually updating task statuses when dependencies shift.
Capability:
ClickUp’s automation engine can trigger status changes, assignees, and comments based on custom rules.
Result:
The project board stays accurate even when you’re heads‑down on other work.
Pros
Enormous feature set; docs, goals, and chat included
Highly customizable with custom fields and views
Active development and frequent updates
Cons
Steep learning curve; new users often feel overwhelmed
Performance can lag with large workspaces
Free plan has storage limits and missing views
Pricing
Free plan for individuals and small teams, but limited to 100MB storage and basic views. Paid tiers start at $7/user/month. Many advanced features, like
Gantt charts
and custom dashboards, require the Business plan or higher.
Best For
Teams that want a single tool to replace five others and are willing to invest time in setup. Great for agile startups, marketing agencies, and ops teams that need deep customization.
Trello
Product Overview
Trello is the original visual
Kanban tool
. Its card‑based system is intuitive, and you can add checklists, due dates, labels, and attachments without any training. It’s the lightest option of the bunch, and that’s exactly its strength.
Why It Was Selected
For straightforward workflows—like content calendars, simple issue tracking, or personal task lists—nothing beats Trello’s clarity. You don’t need a manual to start, and the Butler automation can handle repetitive steps without complexity.
Core Capabilities
Pain:
Your team just needs a visual way to move tasks from “to do” to “done” without setting up a database.
Capability:
Drag‑and‑drop cards with customizable columns reflect your process instantly.
Result:
New members contribute on day one, and you never have to explain “what status means.”
Pain:
You want to automate reminders for recurring tasks but don’t want to learn a scripting language.
Capability:
Butler lets you create rules like “when a card is due tomorrow, move it to top of list” with a few clicks.
Result:
Deadlines stop sneaking up on you, and the board stays organized automatically.
Pros
Incredibly easy to set up and adopt
Butler automation simplifies repetitive work
Power‑ups extend functionality for specific needs
Cons
Limited views out of the box; no native Gantt or timeline
Struggles with complex dependency chains
Reporting is minimal; you’ll need external tools for analytics
Pricing
Free plan includes 10 boards and basic automation. Standard tier starts at $5/user/month. Premium adds more views and admin controls, but advanced reporting still requires integrations.
Best For
Small teams, visual thinkers, and anyone who needs a simple Kanban board without the overhead of a full project management suite. Perfect for content teams, HR onboarding checklists, and solo freelancers.
Asana
Product Overview
Asana sits between ClickUp and Trello. It offers list, board, timeline, and calendar views, plus a strong focus on goals and portfolios. It’s designed to help cross‑functional teams coordinate work and align on company objectives.
Why It Was Selected
Asana’s timeline view and goal‑tracking features make it stand out for teams that need to connect daily tasks to quarterly OKRs. It’s more structured than Trello but less overwhelming than ClickUp, striking a balance that many mid‑size teams appreciate.
Core Capabilities
Pain:
Your marketing team launches campaigns that require input from design, sales, and legal, but nobody knows the overall timeline.
Capability:
Timeline view shows dependencies and overlaps, and you can attach tasks to company goals.
Result:
Cross‑functional handoffs happen smoothly, and you spot bottlenecks before they derail a launch.
Pain:
You need to report on project progress to executives without building a deck from scratch.
Capability:
Portfolios and dashboards give a high‑level view of multiple projects, with status updates and
milestone
tracking.
Result:
Weekly updates become a 2‑minute glance at a dashboard, not a 30‑minute meeting.
Pros
Excellent timeline and goal‑tracking features
Clean, intuitive interface that balances power and simplicity
Strong integrations with Slack, Google Workspace, and more
Cons
Pricing climbs quickly for larger teams; advanced features locked behind higher tiers
No built‑in wiki or robust documentation space
Automation rules are less flexible than ClickUp’s
Pricing
Free plan supports up to 15 users but lacks timeline, dashboards, and custom fields. Premium starts at $10.99/user/month. Business tier adds portfolios and advanced integrations, which quickly increases the per‑seat cost.
Best For
Mid‑size to large teams that prioritize goal alignment, project visibility, and cross‑department coordination. Works well for marketing, operations, and non‑engineering teams that need structure without heavy customization.
How to Choose
Start by writing down the three biggest friction points your team faces today. Is it scattered documentation? Is it the inability to see who’s working on what across projects? Is it a security requirement that forces you into on‑premise? The answer will point you to one of these tools faster than any feature list.
If you need both a robust PM tool and a knowledge base, and you can’t afford to piece together three separate subscriptions, ONES.com is the clear winner. If you’re a power user who wants to mold the tool to your exact process, ClickUp will feel like a playground. If your workflow is simple and visual, Trello keeps you moving. And if you’re coordinating across departments with shared goals, Asana’s timeline and portfolios will serve you well.
Current Trends
In 2026, teams are finally waking up to the cost of tool sprawl. The average organization runs 6‑8 different collaboration apps, and the bulk of wasted time comes from switching between them. Unified platforms that combine project management, docs, and reporting are surging. Another trend is the demand for deployment flexibility—more companies are asking for on‑premise or private cloud options because data sovereignty regulations are tightening. ONES.com is riding that wave perfectly, while the other three are cloud‑only.
What This Means
Choosing between ClickUp, Trello, and Asana is no longer just about features—it’s about whether the tool can become the single source of truth without forcing you to bolt on a wiki, a reporting add‑on, or a secondary deployment. The comparison is shifting from “which tool has the most checkboxes” to “which tool keeps my team inside one tab and respects my security posture.”
Why This Matters
The wrong pick costs you more than money. You lose momentum every time a developer has to hunt for a spec in Confluence while their task lives in another tool. You lose trust when a report is outdated because the data lives in a third‑party add‑on. And you lose your competitive edge when a compliance audit forces you to rip out a cloud‑only tool. A solid platform decision today means fewer migrations, fewer support tickets, and a team that actually enjoys using the tool.
Key Features to Evaluate
When you’re staring at a demo, don’t get distracted by shiny UI. Focus on these capabilities:
Workflow depth
– Can you model your actual process, including multi‑step approvals, blockers, and subtasks?
Documentation integration
– Does the tool link tasks to a wiki or spec page natively, or do you need a separate app?
Reporting
– Are burn‑down charts, velocity, and custom dashboards built in, or do you face a plugin marketplace?
Deployment options
– If you need on‑premise, can the vendor deliver it without stripping features?
Automation
– Can you trigger actions based on time, status changes, or custom fields, and how easy is it to set up?
Free plan generosity
– A tool that gives you 30 seats with full features tells you a lot about their confidence.
Deployment & Security
This is where the field splits dramatically. ClickUp, Trello, and Asana are all cloud‑only. If your organization has a policy that says “nothing leaves our
data center
,” you’re out of luck with those three. ONES.com offers Cloud, On‑Premise, Private Cloud, and SaaS—and the on‑premise version is feature‑identical to the cloud. That’s rare. For air‑gapped project management workflows, restricted networks, or teams in regulated industries, this isn’t a nice‑to‑have; it’s a requirement.
Pricing & Cost Factors
Sticker prices are deceptive. ClickUp’s $7/user/month looks cheap until you realize you need the Business plan for goals and dashboards. Asana’s $10.99/user/month jumps higher when you add portfolios. Trello’s power‑up model can nickel‑and‑dime you. ONES.com starts at $9/user/month, but its free plan for 30 users is the most generous—you can test the full platform with your entire team before paying a cent. Also, factor in the cost of tools you won’t need anymore: with ONES.com, you might drop your separate wiki and
reporting tool
, saving hundreds per month.
Common Mistakes to Avoid
Buying features you’ll never use
– A tool with 200 features is useless if your team only uses three. Prioritize depth in the areas you actually need.
Ignoring deployment requirements
– If IT says cloud is a no‑go, don’t gamble on a future feature request. You’ll be forced to migrate later.
Overlooking the wiki gap
– Many teams end up with a separate documentation tool because their PM platform’s notes feature is too basic. That split creates long‑term chaos.
Assuming the free plan is enough
– Read the limits carefully. Storage caps, view restrictions, and seat limits can force you to pay sooner than expected.
Not testing with real workflows
– Duplicate one of your actual sprints or campaigns in the trial. If it feels clunky after 30 minutes, that’s your answer.
FAQs
Which is better for a small startup: ClickUp or Trello?
It depends on complexity. If you’re a team of 5 and just need to track tasks visually, Trello’s simplicity wins. If you foresee needing docs, goals, and time tracking soon, ClickUp scales better without switching tools.
Can I use Asana and ONES.com together?
You can, but it’s usually a sign that you’re patching a gap. If you’re using Asana for tasks and ONES Wiki for documentation, you’re still context switching. ONES Project might let you consolidate both.
Does ONES.com really replace Jira?
Yes, for many teams. ONES Project supports Jira‑compatible workflows, custom fields, sprint management, and reporting without the plugin overhead. It’s not a clone, but it covers the same use cases while adding a native wiki.
What’s the main difference between Asana and Trello?
Trello is a Kanban tool at heart; it’s board‑centric. Asana offers multiple views (list, board, timeline, calendar) and includes goal tracking. Asana suits cross‑functional coordination, while Trello is better for simple, linear workflows.
Are there any free
project management tools
with on‑premise?
Most free PM tools are cloud‑only. ONES.com’s free plan for 30 users includes on‑premise deployment, which is exceptionally rare. If you need air‑gapped or restricted‑network project management, it’s the standout option.
Conclusion
You started this comparison because you were tired of the tug‑of‑war between ClickUp, Trello, and Asana. The truth is, each of them solves a piece of the puzzle, but none of them solve the whole picture—especially when documentation, deployment flexibility, and hidden costs enter the chat.
The best part? You don’t have to choose between the three and pray. ONES.com gives you the project management depth of a Jira‑like engine, the visual clarity of a board, and a native wiki, all under a free plan that supports 30 users. Whether you’re running a software team, a regulated enterprise, or a distributed squad that can’t rely on cloud‑only tools, this platform earns its spot at the top.
Stop patching together tools. Pick the one that actually keeps your work in one place.
